newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia sets March gathering to promote market.
newsitem.headline: Croatia sets March gathering to promote market.

text.p: Croatia is organising a second international investment gathering, the Financial Forum, to present and promote its expanding capital market on March 5-7.
Three day event, to be located at the central city hotel Intercontinental in capital Zagreb, will feature the central bourse and an over-the-counter market.
The country's leading banks and brokerages, as well as insurers, financial advisers and information suppliers and also expected to present their services to investors, organisers told reporters.
"Although our bourse cannot be compared to that in Chicago, Milan...its role is invaluable," said Nadan Vidosevic, head of the Croatian Chamber of Commerce.
The Zagreb Stock Exchange, trading some 10-15 liquid issues of which two -- Pliva pharmaceutical company and Zagrebacka Banka -- are fully listed, is currently experiencing its second bull run.
The bourse became a hit last year, when turnover soared 70 times to almost one billion kuna ($180 million), after these two very successfully floated their shares at home and abroad.
Pliva became the first Croatian company to get a listing for its global depositary receipts (GDRs) on the London Stock Exchange and Zagrebacka listed its GDRs on Seaq International.
Croatia imposes no tax on capital gains. Corporate profits are taxed at a single rate of 35 percent.
